topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic welcomes the students, introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and contextualises cancer biology across multiple disciplines.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer as a multistep disruption of normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors: invasion, progression, and nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the differences between benign and malignant tumors through their capacity for tissue invasion, their stepwise histological progression, and their standard clinical nomenclature.

topics.label: Pathological mechanisms of cancer-induced disease and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the specific physiological and mechanical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic illness, organ dysfunction, and death.

topics.label: Epidemiological and cross-species incidence of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and tissue distribution of tumors across human populations and compare cancer patterns across companion animals and diverse multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical efficacy of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the diagnostic approaches, benefits, and limitations of screening programs across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic revisits the learning outcomes for student revision and provides logistical framing for upcoming practical sessions and future lectures.
